# v0.30.0-rc1 — nothing lost across retries, replays and restarts

This candidate works toward “nothing lost”: storing each message once across retries, replays and restarts. Each batch of incoming messages commits or rolls back as a unit. The release also preserves more changed history and marks repeated stored copies. Known loss and duplicate-storage limits remain below.

New recall presentation options, entity memory and pre-compaction extraction stay off by default. The next-stage message classifier is planned for v0.30.x. No answer-quality gain is claimed for this release. This candidate starts the v0.30.0 gauntlet; see **Qualification**.

## On by default in this release

- **Atomic ingest with a shadow ledger.** Ingest is the step that stores incoming host messages. Each batch records message bindings, observed timestamps and the conversation view in its own transaction. The shadow ledger records evidence alongside the current message classifier; `LCM_INGEST_LEDGER=off` disables those records without changing stored rows ([#2055](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2055)).

Compaction summarises older context. The fixes under **Changes since v0.29.1** apply without a new setting unless they describe an optional tool or feature. Replay links mark stored copies; a link does not remove either copy.

## Upgrade

- **Host and Python.** Hermes 0.21.3 or newer is required, with 0.21.5 or newer recommended. Python 3.11 or newer is required. Advisory checks against upstream Hermes do not make it a supported host.
- **Store schema.** The schema version stays 5, with no new columns in `messages`. The shadow ledger adds `ledger_meta`, `occurrence_bindings`, `ledger_emissions`, `stamp_observations`, `ingest_views` and `lineage_marks`; recording delegated-child ancestry also adds `session_lineage`. These are additive tables in the existing store ([#2055](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2055)).
- **New settings.** `LCM_INGEST_LEDGER` defaults to `shadow`. The new recall options default to `false` for `recall_adjacent_reply` and `recall_summary_event_time`, `score` for `recall_delivery_order`, and `0` for `recall_snippet_window_hits` and `recall_extra_entries`; their environment variables and effects are under **Optional features**. Upgrading from v0.29.1 also brings v0.29.2's `LCM_SHUTDOWN_COMPACTION_WAIT_S` (default 10 s).
- **Removed condensation and transcript cleanup.** Cache-friendly follow-on condensation and transcript garbage collection are removed. `LCM_CACHE_FRIENDLY_CONDENSATION_ENABLED` and `LCM_LARGE_OUTPUT_TRANSCRIPT_GC_ENABLED` remain parsed but are ignored, with one warning per process when enabled. Existing garbage-collection placeholders remain readable ([#1246](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1246)).
- **Deferred maintenance is deprecated.** `LCM_DEFERRED_MAINTENANCE_ENABLED` still works and defaults to off, but enabling it adds a warning in `/lcm status`, `lcm_status` and the `lcm_doctor` configuration check. Removal is planned for v0.31.0. `LCM_DEFERRED_MAINTENANCE_MAX_PASSES` applies only while it is enabled ([#1246](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1246)).
- **Host message identifiers stay in shadow.** `LCM_HOST_MESSAGE_UID` defaults to `shadow`. The next-stage classifier and its identifier-based decisions remain planned for v0.30.x.
- **Rollback.** Take a SQLite-safe backup before upgrading. The rollback target is v0.29.2 (or v0.29.1 until v0.29.2 is released).

## Changes since v0.29.1

This release also contains every v0.29.2 fix, including the new `LCM_SHUTDOWN_COMPACTION_WAIT_S` setting (default 10 s). They are described in the v0.29.2 notes and not repeated here.

### Restarts, retries and replay links

- **Compaction snapshots survive carry updates.** Maintaining carried message ranges keeps the record of message occurrences tied to its compaction proof. After a restart, an equal-content retry with a changed timestamp or message ID is still stored ([#1451](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1451)).
- **Recovered user turns have visible replay copies.** After a restart, possible replay copies of a recovered user turn are marked. New requests with the same text remain stored ([#1523](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1523)).
- **Failed identity reads retry classification.** If an identity-anchor read or timestamp backfill fails after the host changed messages before the resume point, ingest rolls back and classifies once more. A persistent fault keeps the previous fallback, and a busy retry remains available; no row is lost ([#1815](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1815)).
- **A replayed tool result is stored once.** After a restart, a resume point between a stored call and its result no longer causes the result to be stored twice. The skip requires an identical, directly following stored result, matching timestamps and an unused earlier occurrence; results without that evidence are stored ([#2163](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2163)).
- **Ambiguous restart copies are marked.** When a restart re-sends an already stored batch from the start, each repeated row gets a `possible_replay_of` link to the oldest unused matching row in the same session. Matching tries exact content before content with reasoning blocks removed, and refuses different known timestamps. Exact copies made only of reasoning blocks are linked too ([#2305](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2305), [#588](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/588)).
- **Rotation replay links cross the recorded chain.** After a fit-only session rotation that has no child commit proof, a cold resend still stores earlier sessions’ rows again, but now links each copy to its earlier row, except the re-emitted summary marker, which has no saved original. Linking checks the current session first and stays within the conversation’s recorded ancestors. For a 32-hop chain and 2,000-row resend, the write-lock hold rose from 183 ms to 272 ms at the 90th percentile; median ingest time was 1.58 times `v0.29.2-rc1` in that benchmark ([#2029](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2029)).
- **Changed timestamps keep their provenance.** Re-stamped carried turns link to their earlier occurrences after compaction and rotation, including originals in a predecessor session and first copies stored by a rotation child. Prompts that inherited a carried timestamp, or were later stored at their own timestamp, also get links. Rows with the same replay identity but different content link to their own originals ([#2378](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2378), [#2390](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2390)).
- **Borrowed timestamps get a replay link.** When the host shows the next user prompt with the timestamp of the prompt in flight during compaction, the later stored copy gets one `possible_replay_of` link. The earlier copy remains available for other replay links; neither row is skipped or changed.
- **Each copy gets one replay link.** The cursor-zero replay scan and session ancestry adoption no longer add a second replay link to a row already linked by an earlier step ([#2305](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2305)).
- **An interrupted helper agent keeps its rows.** A delegated child that is interrupted before it finishes now keeps its rows up to its last completed save, which runs before each of its model calls. This covers every helper agent that runs its own LCM-X engine, as helper agents do on the supported Hermes versions, while that engine still serves the profile the helper agent started with; otherwise its rows are saved only when it finishes, as before, and one WARNING says so. Before this release, an interrupted child kept none of its rows ([#2482](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2482)).

### Compaction and changed history

- **Delegated children no longer lose a new row when the compression boundary is missing.** After a failed pre-compaction store, a failed boundary record or a concurrent store, a later row that repeats the last stored row no longer causes a new row to be lost. A child resumes at its last stored row only when all preceding rows are stored in its ancestry or are outputs of its last compaction. It stores other preceding rows along with the later rows and warns with their count. The compaction-output record is kept only in memory, so after a restart the child's compacted head is stored one extra time (a duplicate; nothing is lost). A new row with the same content and role as an older stored row still cannot be told apart from it; other limits are under **Known issues** ([#2071](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2071)).
- **Busy pre-compaction writes skip the pass.** If a delegated child cannot store its input because the database is locked or busy, compaction returns `noop` with `compaction skipped: input not stored`. The next pass stores the full view first. Other write failures still lose rows removed by compaction, as disclosed under **Known issues** ([#2306](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2306), [#2440](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2440)).
- **Moved tool rows are stored within a bounded history.** When the host changes messages before the resume point and the audit also finds a missing row there, LCM-X stores moved tool calls and their results. This applies to standard tool-call records across the session and its verified or recorded predecessors, within 10,000 stored rows, 15 million stored-text bytes and 10,000 tool-call entries. All three bounds must hold; the remaining shapes are listed under **Known issues** ([#2455](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2455), [#2467](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2467)).
- **Host folds and task-list snapshots replay safely.** Assistant folds anchored to stored parts and unstamped task-list snapshots already held in the session are recognised as replays, including batches replayed from the start. Original bytes and timestamped user snapshots stay stored; ambiguous or over-budget shapes remain new. Treating an unstamped task-list block as generated host text requires timestamped-prompt evidence, and later edits and proven rewinds survive optional-read failures.
- **Task-list provenance survives session end.** Exact task-list snapshot replays after session-end flushes get links without suppressing new snapshots. Stored host task-list composites record ordered `composite_of` provenance when their whole-row decomposition is unique, without changing ingest or replay decisions. After a conversation ends and resumes, a to-do list merged with your next message is not linked yet; see Known issues ([#2488](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2488)).
- **Ignored-message placeholders stay out of stored history.** A compaction pass clears its message-to-store-ID map when it finishes. A later ingest can no longer mistake a reused memory address for that old mapping and store a carried ignored-message placeholder as a real row ([#2344](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2344)).
- **Merged human text stays visible.** On hosts without a model-only display key, LCM-X clears a stale `model_only` marker from generated rows in a mixed user group. The merged human text stays visible ([#1436](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1436)).

### Recall and tools

- **Memory names advertise their existing limit.** The `lcm_memory` schema now states the 256-character limit on `name` and each `aliases` entry. The tool already enforced this limit ([#1944](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1944)).
- **Read-only store access over MCP.** `scripts/lcm_x_mcp.py` (the `lcm-x mcp` reader) serves `lcm_recall`, `lcm_grep`, `lcm_expand`, `lcm_load_session` and `lcm_describe` to Claude Code through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) over standard input and output. It needs a source checkout of this repository, because a catalog install does not include `scripts/`. Register it with `claude mcp add` and the Hermes venv Python (3.10 or newer); see the operator guide. It opens one Hermes store read-only per call, uses production schemas and outputs, and returns `store_uuid` plus degraded-mode flags. Unless a writer stamped an ID, it derives one from file identity and reports `store_uuid_source: derived`; it does not alter Hermes stores ([#1192](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1192)).

### Operator tools and diagnostics

- **Doctor and backup respect ingest transactions.** `/lcm doctor clean apply`, `/lcm doctor repair apply`, backup flushes and doctor full-text-search integrity checks take the store write lock. They wait for a multi-row ingest to commit instead of rolling back or partly committing its rows ([#2345](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2345)).
- **Pending raw-flush counts are explicit.** The session-end warning reports `unflushed=unknown` while the ingest cursor awaits reconciliation. The count is described as a cursor-based estimate, rather than a durability count ([#1364](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1364)).
- **Session decisions and storing routes are logged.** Per-engine INFO logs identify binding and bypass rules and the first store or skip, without message or pattern text. Every ingest that stores rows also emits a content-free `LCM ingest route:` line ([#2042](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2042), [#2305](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2305)).
- **Successful child resumes stop reporting false fallbacks.** Successful delegated-child resumes and store-only turns log at DEBUG. They no longer add false fallback counts or skipped-ingest warnings; storage is unchanged ([#2074](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2074)).

### Integration documentation

- **Companion hook timing is scoped to its evidence.** The separate Claude Code integration’s 0.1.0 notes distinguish drain time, pointer-file stalls and hooks stopped by the host. They scope measured figures to the recorded runs and point to the release’s own result card. They also clarify search modes, configuration-dependent paths, local cleanup audit fields and temporary-file handling ([#2350](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2350)).


## Optional features

- **Adjacent replies in recall.** `recall_adjacent_reply` / `LCM_RECALL_ADJACENT_REPLY` defaults to `false`. Enabling it places next-turn replies after the best raw recall hit and the top three question hits, within existing hit and size caps. It is read-only and deadline-bounded; internal recall and session delivery keep their behaviour.
- **Summary event-time ranges.** `recall_summary_event_time` / `LCM_RECALL_SUMMARY_EVENT_TIME` defaults to `false`. `lcm.recall_summary_event_time: true` in `config.yaml` also enables it, with the environment taking precedence. Model-called `lcm_recall` summary hits and session-delivery summary leads get `event_time_start` and `event_time_end` from source messages’ earliest and latest host `observed_at`, including condensed sources. It never uses write times. The fields are absent when no source has a host time. A carried timestamp adds `time_uncertain: "carried"`. A non-strict `answer_ready` summary then stops taking a message’s `event_time`. Failed or late reads set `provenance.summary_event_time_unavailable`. Internal recall and benchmark output keep their behaviour.
- **Recall hits in time order.** `recall_delivery_order` / `LCM_RECALL_DELIVERY_ORDER` defaults to `score`. Set it to `time` to deliver the same selected `lcm_recall` hits from oldest to newest by host observation time, with untimed hits and summaries last. Session delivery and internal recall keep their existing order.
- **Wider recall snippets.** `recall_snippet_window_hits` / `LCM_RECALL_SNIPPET_WINDOW_HITS` defaults to `0`. The first N message-excerpt hits get windows of up to 2,400 characters, centred on the matched chunk, keyword match or query match. Shorter messages return whole. Ranking, selection, proactive recall, `detail="answer_ready"` and `delivery_unit="session"` keep their behaviour. Larger windows can fit fewer hits under `response_char_cap`, reported as `response_cap_truncated`. Failed or late window reads retain the original snippet and set `snippet_window_skipped` to `read_error` or `deadline`.
- **Compact extra recall entries.** `recall_extra_entries` / `LCM_RECALL_EXTRA_ENTRIES` defaults to `0` and is capped at 25. Snippet-hit delivery appends at most the smaller of that cap and half the delivered limit, rounded down, as 300-character extras from later ranks. It skips duplicates without refill. The candidate pool, rerank window and `total_results` keep their existing sizes. Extras carry only `kind`, `store_id`, `session_id`, `event_time`, `window` and `extra=true`. Late or failed reads set `extra_entries_skipped` to `deadline` or `read_error`. Internal recall, answer-ready and session delivery ignore the setting.
- **Extraction stops at its deadline.** Pre-compaction extraction, `LCM_EXTRACTION_ENABLED` / `extraction_enabled`, still defaults to `false`. Its absolute deadline now also bounds the host stream, so a slowly streaming extraction stops at that deadline ([#1149](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1149)).
- **Event recorder.** `LCM_RECORDER_ENABLED` defaults to `false`. Enabling it writes what the host asks of LCM-X to local files under `LCM_RECORDER_DIR` (default `$HERMES_HOME/lcm-recorder/`), so a run can be replayed offline against another build. All recorder writes are capped by `LCM_RECORDER_MAX_BYTES` (default 20 GiB). Restart the host to change these settings. The recorder needs Python 3.12 or newer; on Python 3.11 the flag logs one warning and installs nothing ([#2243](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2243)).

## Known issues

Loss limits come first. Fixes are planned for v0.30.x unless a different release is named. “Resume point” means the position through which LCM-X believes it has already examined the host’s messages.

- **An interrupted helper agent can lose the rows after its last save.** A helper agent's rows are saved before each of its model calls. If the process ends before the next save, the rows since the last one are not saved. This happens while its tools run: that round's tool call and finished results stay only in the host's database. It also happens while a save waits more than 5 seconds on a busy database at shutdown, and then one WARNING gives the number of rows not yet saved. Every earlier row is saved for a helper agent that runs its own LCM-X engine, while that engine still serves the profile the helper agent started with. Otherwise, and for a helper agent without its own engine, the rows not yet saved are saved only when the helper agent finishes, so an interruption loses them, as before this release. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2482](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2482), [#2483](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2483)).
- **New messages after a host-shortened history are lost.** If the host shortens the conversation on its own, such as an undo followed by a compression request that compacts nothing, later new messages are treated as already stored and are not saved. Which hosts produce this shape is not established. A second known route is Hermes's message-sequence repair, which runs only when message alternation is broken and rewrites the list in place: if LCM-X ingests the repaired, shorter list before the next new message, that next user message is not stored. No run has shown this route yet. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1525](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1525)).
- **Repeated text is under-stored on partial-history hosts.** After a restart and compaction, a host that sends only new messages loses occurrences of text repeated within the session. The reference agent sends full history. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2124](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2124)).
- **Repeated compacted-out tool pairs are lost.** On hosts that reuse tool-call IDs, a new call and result identical to a pair compacted out of view are treated as a replay after a cold restart and are not stored. The already-shipped fix for a pair still in view does not cover this shape. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2172](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2172)).
- **Busy session end with undo and resend leaves a message unstored.** With ignore patterns configured, a busy session end followed by undo, resend and an ingest that changes nothing leaves the earlier occurrence pending and counted at exit, but not stored ([#2247](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2247)). Separately, without ignore patterns, any busy session end followed by an undo and resend also keeps the earlier occurrence pending, counted and reported at exit rather than stored. Only a host resume of that session recovers it; `/new` does not. ([#1838](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1838), [#2206](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2206)). Planned fix: v0.30.x.
- **An ignored-message placeholder makes a later loss silent.** If ignore patterns are or were configured and the session-end view contains an LCM-X ignored-message placeholder, a busy session end followed by undo and resend loses the earlier occurrence. Session end logs a pending retry, but the later drop is neither counted nor reported. v0.29.x lost the same message on this trigger but warned at session end that final messages might be missing; this release no longer gives that warning. No ignore patterns are set by default. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2474](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2474)).
- **Untimestamped replacements before the resume point are lost.** A host merge or replacement before the resume point drops an unstamped new row; if an entirely unstamped view replaces all rows at the same length, none of the new rows is stored. On Hermes this follows undoing every turn or retrying a one-turn session when no host database exists or its transcript write failed; timestamped rows are stored. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#7](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/7)).
- **Some moved tool rows are still skipped.** A moved tool call or result before the resume point is not rescued when the audit finds no missing row there. The audit never examines tool rows on its own: a tool call and result replaced before the resume point are lost, and a pair inserted there stores its result without its call ([#2452](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2452)). Tool groups that cross the resume point while their unstamped results were already stored also retain the old skip behaviour. Affected new rows are not stored; planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2455](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2455), [#2467](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2467)).
- **Large or non-standard tool histories keep the old loss behaviour.** The moved-tool check does not run beyond 10,000 stored rows, 15 million bytes of stored text or 10,000 tool-call entries across the session and its ancestry. It also falls back for the whole scope if any stored tool-call format is non-standard: call entries must be objects with text IDs and text arguments. New moved rows left classified as positional replays are not stored, and one INFO line reports the limit; planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2455](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2455), [#2467](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2467)).
- **Externalized arguments and reused IDs bypass the moved-tool fix.** A call whose arguments are externalized at ingest reads as a reused ID, including an inline data URI with at least 256 base64 characters, a run of at least 4,096 base64-alphabet characters, or line-wrapped base64. Reused IDs, repeated call or result IDs in the view, and argument comparisons beyond the 256,000-byte parsing budget retain the old replay decision, leaving affected new call or result rows unstored. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2172](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2172), [#2467](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2467)).
- **Replaced unstamped replies and scaffold-looking replies are lost.** If a reply reaches LCM-X without its host timestamp and the host replaces it before the resume point (an edit-and-resend in a long session), the replacement is not stored while the session runs. A restart stores it, together with copies of the session's other unstamped replies ([#2479](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2479)). Replies that carry their host timestamp, as Hermes sends them unless a session has no host database or a transcript write failed, are stored. Planned fix for this part: v0.31 ([#2116](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2116)). A reply carrying `CONTEXT SUMMARY` markers is still treated as LCM-X scaffold while the engine is running, and lossy-redacted rows still count as replays. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2467](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2467)).
- **Unreadable ancestry limits moved-row recovery.** If presence reads fail, ancestry cannot be verified with `state.db` present, or a rotation-predecessor write failed in the current process, only rows found by the existing audit are stored. Other rows before the resume point remain classified as replays and affected new rows are not stored; a warning reports the fallback. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2467](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2467)).
- **Identifier-only replacements behind a merged summary are lost.** When the host changes only a message’s unique ID behind an unchanged merged scaffold, the cached prefix consumes the proof and the replacement is not stored. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1428](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1428)).
- **A new occurrence at an alternate timestamp is lost.** Once the original host view is gone, a new event with identical content at a previously recorded alternate timestamp is not stored. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1519](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1519)).
- **Earlier edits inside a shortened view are lost.** If a host shortens its view and edits an earlier row in place, LCM-X does not store that edit. This also occurs in v0.27.0. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1563](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1563)).
- **A retried result with only a new ID is lost.** After a cold restart, a retried tool result whose only change is its unique message ID is dropped. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1837](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1837)).
- **Identical new tool pairs after restart are lost.** A new call and result identical to an earlier stored pair are treated as a replay after restart and are not stored. If the restart follows a stored rewrite of the earlier result, the old call is also stored again beside that rewritten result without a replay link. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2377](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2377), [#2414](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2414)).
- **Pasted scaffold-shaped user turns are lost.** A user turn that starts with the preserved-objective prefix or quotes a whole summary part is skipped when there is no current version-4 compaction proof, including before any compaction, under older proofs or after a cold rebind retires a stale proof. A task-list-prefix turn is affected in every proof state; before any compaction, such turns are skipped after restart even at the tail, or while running when before a stored row. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2110](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2110), [#2418](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2418)).
- **Equal user identities hide a new occurrence.** With many equal user-message identities, a recorded boundary that becomes ambiguous on the next view lets an older copy count against a new one. One occurrence is not stored. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2422](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2422)).
- **A warm view that starts with a tool call can store nothing.** When a warm ingest gets a view that starts with a tool call and does not extend the previous view, none of its rows is stored. No host path is known to produce this view. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2419](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2419)).
- **Non-busy pre-compaction write failures lose child rows.** When a delegated child’s input write fails for a reason other than a locked or busy database, such as a disk or I/O error, compaction still removes rows from its view and those raw rows are lost. Their stored summary is the only trace, and `compression boundary not recorded: input not stored` warns about the failure. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2440](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2440)).
- **Multiple timestamp conflicts after busy session end lose messages.** After a busy session end with no later ingest, two or more messages whose host timestamps conflict with saved copies can be lost. If a later ingest brings the same messages unchanged, they are kept and counted instead. v0.29.2 has the same limit. Planned fix: v0.30.x.
- **A same-second resend under a new platform ID is lost.** After a cold restart, a new turn with the same text in the same second as an earlier one, under a new platform ID, is taken as the earlier turn and is not stored. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1037](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1037)).
- **A repeated tool step after a rewind can be missed, with an identical message after it.** After a restart, if a conversation was rewound and the agent repeats exactly the same tool call with the same result, followed by a message identical to an earlier saved one, all three are taken as a replay and are not saved, even when the host's timestamps show they are new. We know of no way to trigger this from Hermes today. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2259](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2259)).
- **One half of a re-dated tool pair can be saved without the other.** After a restart in a conversation that LCM-X has compacted, if the host re-dates only one half of a saved tool call and its result as new, that half is saved and its partner is not. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2191](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2191)).
- **Messages pending at a busy session end are missing after a gateway stop until you resume.** If a session end found the database busy and the gateway stops before a retry succeeds, the messages still pending are missing from the store until you resume that conversation. After /new they are not recovered. The only sign is the warning logged when the session ended. The fix needs a change in Hermes ([#2253](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2253)).
- **Messages can be missing if the database stays busy from a session end until the process ends.** If the database is busy when a session ends, stays busy at every later retry (the next session start or end, a related session's start, and the 5-second shutdown drain), and the process then dies or exits while it is still busy, the session's last messages are not saved. They are saved only if you resume that conversation; /new does not recover them. Every busy session end and every failed retry is logged and counted. This is an accepted limit; fixing it needs a journal outside the database.
- **A few restart cases keep messages pending instead of saving them.** After a busy session end, LCM-X keeps a conversation's newest messages pending, rather than risk saving them in the wrong place, in three more cases: a single message that the host re-dates newer than its saved copy; a view rewritten after later messages were saved; and, when the session's binding is ignored or stateless, a message with a different known timestamp. Pending messages are counted and reported when the process exits, but they are saved only if you resume that conversation. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1838](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1838)).
- **An identical message re-sent in place is taken as a replay.** On hosts that send no message IDs or timestamps, a message re-sent with exactly the same text in the same place, so the conversation does not get longer, cannot be told apart from a replay, and it is not saved again. The same holds when a shortened conversation grows back with identical messages, and for identical overlapping messages in a migration or a full-history replay. This is a design limit: telling them apart needs message IDs or timestamps from the host.
- **Some Desktop sessions can end with nothing saved.** Some sessions started from the Desktop app can end with no messages saved. The cause is not known yet; this release logs each session's storing decision to help find it. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2042](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2042)).

The remaining limits store extra copies, leave attribution incomplete or fail to honour an exclusion rule. They do not lose raw rows.

- **Some excluded parents still have stored children.** After an excluded parent rotates through compression, its delegated child is refused only on the shared route. Clone and prototype routes store the child despite `LCM_IGNORE_SESSION_PATTERNS` or the stateless exclusion patterns. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2070](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2070)).
- **Failed pre-compaction storage also duplicates a head.** After a failed input write before compaction, LCM-X stores the compacted head once more without a replay relation. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2440](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2440)).
- **Repeated recovery stores a user row again.** Two recovery fits of a repeated user turn followed by a restart store the projected user row once more, without a replay relation. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#503](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/503)).
- **A later child restart stores kept rows again.** After rejecting a delegated child’s last-stored-row resume boundary, an identical rewritten view stores kept rows again without a replay relation. This takes one restart after a warm rejection or a second restart after a cold rejection; delegated-child restart resume is not reachable on the current host. The record of a child's last compaction outputs is also kept only in memory, so a restart of a delegated child stores its compacted head one extra time. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2439](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2439)).
- **Routing-key changes store the history again.** If the host assigns a live session a new routing key, such as a CLI handoff or resume from another room, the next warm turn stores the whole history again under the new conversation ID without replay relations. This was found in clone-run preflight and code reading and is not yet reproduced on main. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2461](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2461)).
- **Missing compression ancestry duplicates carried rows.** When a compression child’s ancestry cannot be verified and the host inserts a row before the resume point, the next ingest stores the parent’s final prompt and reply again without replay relations. This includes missing host state, missing parent or child records, a parent that did not end by compression or a fork marker; apparently complete ancestry also fails when an earlier process never wrote a needed predecessor record. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2463](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2463)).
- **A merged summary carrier creates an extra copy.** After the host merges LCM-X’s summary carrier into a user row, a warm replay from the start stores the merged carrier again, or stores copies from an otherwise unchanged view plus appended rows. Other middle-of-history edits do not belong to this limit. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1961](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1961)).
- **An unstamped restart replay stores old rows again.** The first ingest after restart can store another copy while advancing past a replayed prefix. This limit requires matching earlier rows in order, an earlier timestamped copy and a new copy with `observed_at` NULL; replay from position zero is handled by the new replay-link fix. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1674](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1674)).
- **A rewritten unstamped view is stored again.** An ended engine’s final flush stores an unstamped view again after a resumed engine rewrites it, or a rewrite after a cold-start retry is stored again. A view with an additional host insertion or reordering is outside this limit. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2203](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2203)).
- **An unanswered prompt becomes part of a composite.** After a restart before the reply, the unanswered prompt and the next prompt are stored together as a composite row beside the next prompt’s own row. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#849](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/849)).
- **Rotation mapping can stall compaction.** A rotation leaves rows without the mapping compaction needs, so compaction stops making progress. A cold resend after a held fit-only rotation also stores predecessor rows again; those copies now carry `possible_replay_of` links across the recorded rotation chain, except the re-emitted summary marker. Planned fix for the remaining mapping and store-growth limits: v0.30.x ([#2029](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2029)).
- **Unstamped histories with existing copies grow on every restart.** On a host that sends no message timestamps, a session that already holds later exact copies of some rows stores its replayed history once more at each restart. Each extra copy has a possible-replay link. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#588](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/588)).
- **Earlier ledger-off copies cannot anchor borrowed-timestamp links.** Borrowed-timestamp linking cannot see a copy stored while `LCM_INGEST_LEDGER` was off. It can therefore link to a different bound copy when complete bindings would have left the attribution ambiguous; no row or per-key count changes. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2443](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2443)).
- **A late tool call stores its result twice.** When a tool call's row was not stored at its turn, a later ingest that brings the call (typically after a restart or a rebind, when the host sends its full history) stores the call once and its result a second time, without a replay relation. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2468](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2468)).
- **A persistent evidence fault can store the last row again.** After an evidence-read fault that persists past its retry (or a busy error followed by a one-off evidence-read fault, which gets no retry), the fail-open path can store the already-stored last row once more, shifted by a timestamped insert before it. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2374](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2374)).
- **Unstamped reply histories are stored again after an edit-and-resend and a restart.** On a host that sends replies without timestamps, a cold restart after an edit-and-resend stores the session's whole unstamped reply history again (41 copies after 40 turns in our test), without replay relations. Replies with host timestamps are not affected, and v0.29.1 and v0.29.2 behave the same. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2479](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2479)).
- **A restart right after a fit-only compaction can save the summary again.** After a compaction that only trimmed the conversation to fit, if the host keeps the trimmed list and the agent restarts before LCM-X next saves the session, one extra copy of LCM-X's summary joined to the first kept message can be saved as a plain message. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2118](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2118)).
- **A to-do list merged with your next message can be saved again.** The host can merge a saved to-do list with your next message into one combined message. When that combined message splits cleanly into earlier saved messages of the same session, LCM-X now links it to them with `composite_of`. After a conversation ends and resumes, though, the combined message is saved again with no link. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2488](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2488)).
- **A message can be saved twice after certain compaction passes.** After an overflow-recovery pass, or a compaction whose compacted messages were all hidden ones, if the host commits the rewritten conversation and restarts before the next compaction, a message can be saved again with no replay link. This has not been reproduced yet. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2134](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2134)).
- **A reused tool-call ID far apart can save a pair twice after a restart.** If a session reuses a tool-call ID for the same call and result more than 64 saved rows later, a restart can save that pair a second time without a replay link. No natural way to trigger this has been shown; our test forces it. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2197](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2197)).
- **A failed hand-off read can save a carried message again.** If LCM-X cannot read the previous session's record during a hand-off, a carried-over message can be saved again without a replay link. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2490](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2490)).
- **A kept message with a model-switch note can be saved again.** After a compaction, when the conversation is picked up again, a kept message that starts with a model-switch note and is shown with an extra leading space can be saved again, along with the next carried-over message. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2431](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2431)).
- **Older databases without conversation IDs can save a tool pair twice.** On older databases with no conversation IDs recorded, a tool call and its result can be saved twice after a restart. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2436](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2436)).
- **An insert into a just-compacted conversation can save the latest reply again.** If the app inserts a message without a timestamp into a conversation that a compaction has just moved to a new session, and the latest reply also has no timestamp, LCM-X can save that reply a second time. Without the app's session database, the carried-over earlier prompts can be saved again too. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2491](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2491), [#2463](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2463)).
- **A few compaction and setting-change paths save a marked extra copy.** After certain compactions, a restart can save LCM-X's summary or the compacted input again, marked as a copy: when the compaction's saved record is out of date, when a compaction that moved the conversation to a new session (a non-default setting) is followed by a restart before the new session starts, or when a restart comes before a new compaction is adopted. Changing the redaction setting before LCM-X first saves a session with the ingest ledger on can also save one marked extra copy, once. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#1286](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1286), [#758](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/758)).

Duplicate attribution requires the recorded ingest route and both store IDs; restart replay also requires the restart record. Timestamp absence alone does not establish a cause.

One more limit affects only what the model sees in its prompt; no stored row is lost or copied.

- **Turns can drop out of the prompt for up to 10 minutes after rejected summaries.** If two summaries in a row are rejected and the maintenance sweep runs out of time, turns that no summary covers yet can be missing from the model's prompt for up to 600 seconds. They stay stored, and the next successful summary covers them. Planned fix: v0.30.x ([#2272](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2272)).

## Qualification

This is a release candidate for testing. It is not qualified for general use yet, and v0.29.1 remains the latest stable release. As a minor release, v0.30.0 runs a smoke stage at this rc and then the full gauntlet. GA needs every gate below.

- Nothing lost, the certifying driven run (r9, on this rc's product code): **PASS: 0 lost rows and 0 silent copies; all 13 extra copies are visible** ([receipt](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1931#issuecomment-6722263492)). The earlier run, r8, on the same product code, lost no rows but failed the silent-copy bar: 7 to-do-merged copies carried a `composite_of` link that the written rule did not yet count ([r8 verdict](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1931#issuecomment-6720266640)). [#2495](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2495) wrote the rule down before r9, and r8 keeps its verdict.
- Full suite, the CI way, at the rc tag: **TBD**.
- Smoke stage at this rc:
  - reliability matrix on all seven hosts, gating on new failures: **TBD**;
  - the 12 hands-on fault-cell pairs, with no unmatched failure: **TBD**;
  - Phase A, every registered tool in both postures: **TBD**;
  - upgrade, rollback and re-upgrade on one store copy, with 0 lost and 0 duplicated rows: **TBD**;
  - D1 recall with embeddings off, fast tier: 0 unexplained per-question changes: **TBD**;
  - Phase B, the independent review sweep of the full diff: **TBD**.
- Full rows: D1 to D8, the D5 reference-agent window and the D5 real-store clone run: **TBD**.
- Matched previous-GA disposition ([#2212](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2212)): not measured as a verdict in this release. The kit records plain counts for every test cell. The breakdowns by logger and by event, and the count of events that could not be tied to a session, ship in v0.30.x.
- D7, the compaction row (how often compaction runs, how long turns wait, rows kept through compaction, and facts kept against the previous release): **not run at this rc**, although the release spec runs D7 at every rc1. Its facts bar needs a floor measured with a reader bridge, which moves to v0.30.x ([#2492](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2492)). The fallback that would have judged its other bars without that floor left a run mode that could exit 0 with no verdict, so under exits declared before the #2492 bridge reviews, the D7 row does not run for this rc. The design document keeps D7's turn-wait bars in the v0.30.0 gate, so GA needs a D7 run on a later rc; shipping without any of D7's bars would need an explicit release-spec exception first.
